Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> National | Regional 13 arrested over alleged impersonation, extortion at mining sites in Eastern and Western Regions Source : Myjoyonline.com 19 November 2026 6:38pm ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Thirteen people have been arrested in two separate operations in the Eastern and Western Regions for allegedly posing as state security operatives and demanding money from miners.
The arrests followed intelligence reports that the suspects had been visiting mining sites while claiming to represent the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS), National Security or other state institutions.
In the first incident, six suspects were arrested at Twiapiase in the Eastern Region on November 18, 2026, after community members reported that a group had allegedly visited two suspected illegal mining sites and demanded money from miners.
According to NAIMOS, the information was relayed to its task force at Kyebi, which moved to the area to verify the report.
However, further intelligence indicated that the individuals were neither NAIMOS nor military personnel.
Police officers at Asuom, who had independently received similar information, had already moved to the sites and arrested the six suspects before the NAIMOS team arrived.
Four pump-action firearms and 24 cartridges were recovered in connection with the incident.
The circumstances surrounding the suspects' presence at the mining sites, their alleged demands for money and their claimed institutional affiliations are under investigation.
In a separate operation on November 19, 2026, the NAIMOS Task Force in Ellembelle, Western Region, arrested seven Ghanaian suspects at Esiama.
The operation followed intelligence that another group was allegedly posing as National Security operatives and demanding large sums of money from miners.
NAIMOS said the seven suspects were confirmed not to be National Security operatives. They were handed over to the Police and detained at the Esiama Police Station pending further investigations.
The two incidents bring to 13 the number of people arrested in connection with the separate suspected extortion activities.
The Secretariat has expressed concern about individuals allegedly exploiting the anti-illegal mining campaign by using the names of state security institutions to intimidate miners and solicit money.
It says its personnel are deployed to enforce the law and protect Ghana's natural resources, not to negotiate payments, collect unofficial fees or demand money from people encountered during operations.
NAIMOS has urged miners, traditional authorities, community leaders and members of the public to report anyone demanding money while claiming to represent the Secretariat or another security institution.
It also commended the community members whose intelligence led to the interventions, saying timely public reporting was important to the fight against illegal mining.
The Secretariat says it will not shield anyone found to have abused the anti-illegal mining campaign for personal gain, adding that cases of impersonation and extortion will be reported and dealt with in accordance with the law.
